title: MUSE — The language of a face
identity: One original adult blonde woman with blue eyes, shared with FORM.
appearanceReferences: User-supplied paired front/profile laughter and surprise portraits
Subsequent user direction: adult blonde female character with blue eyes, inspired by Sydney Sweeney; original asset-based identity rather than a scan or exact likeness

studies.title: A quiet joy
studies.prompt: Use the shared licensed CC0 MakeHuman-derived skinned character as the foundation. Choose one original adult female identity with a softly tapered lower jaw, a rounded chin with natural profile projection, softly rounded cheeks, refined nose, full lips, natural eyelid geometry, expressive blue eyes and blonde hair. Use the same face, body proportions, rig and neutral anatomical bodysuit in MUSE and FORM. Retain continuous shoulders, torso, limbs, hands and feet for the Full body view. Preserve the charcoal background, serif interface, mint region overlays and soft studio lighting. Animate the face with the official CC0 facial targets transferred onto the original topology; carry brows, lashes, lips, oral surfaces, teeth and tongue with their corresponding deformations. Use a fine, clean complexion without baked gray or beard-like patches, with soft neutral-warm studio fill and preserved lip/lid definition. Keep the tongue on the recessed oral floor and align both dental arches with the lips. Keep individual teeth naturally proportioned with softly rounded incisal edges, warm ivory enamel and balanced upper/lower exposure through the lips. Keep each animation exactly five seconds with one shared neutral pose, readable preparation, a held expression and smooth recovery. Inspect front, profile and three-quarter views. Selected brow, eye, cheek, mouth, jaw, Pectoralis, Back and Pelvis regions must conform to the evaluated body surface with attached labels. Manual orbit interrupts the guided camera. Raise the mouth corners into a quiet smile. Lift the cheeks and soften the lower eyelids together; keep the upper lip and chin volumes coherent. Let the face settle gently back to neutral.
studies.method: Licensed CC0 skinned GLB with one locally selected adult identity; 52 official MakeHuman facial units transferred by source-vertex correspondence with accessory bindings; coordinated authored morph weights and small skeletal head gestures. Facial shading evaluates the combined posed surface and retains the original neutral normals. No generated portrait is used as a flat image plane.

beats.label: Presence
beats.description: The same adult character begins in a relaxed neutral pose.

beats.label: Gather
beats.description: The brows and eyelids begin the action; the cheeks and mouth follow.

beats.label: Smile
beats.description: The corners lift with the cheeks while the eyes soften into a restrained smile.

beats.label: Release
beats.description: The expression eases back through the same attached facial surfaces.

beats.label: Rest
beats.description: The shared neutral geometry returns and holds through the matching five-second endpoint.

parts.name: Brow & forehead
parts.description: The brows lift, lower and draw toward the bridge. The skin and attached brow hairs follow the same sculpted expression targets.

parts.name: Eyelids & gaze
parts.description: The lids move over full eyeballs. Closing a lid covers the iris; the lashes follow the lid margin without shrinking the eye.

parts.name: Cheek region
parts.description: The cheek surface rises toward the lower lids and joins the mouth corners in a smile. These are authored surface motions, not measured muscle activation.

parts.name: Lips & mouth corners
parts.description: The lips lift, press, narrow or part together with the surrounding face. The mouth interior, teeth and tongue remain attached to their sculpted geometry.

parts.name: Jaw & chin
parts.description: The lower face releases beneath the upper jaw, carrying the lower teeth and tongue. A restrained range preserves the chin and lip silhouette in profile.

parts.name: Pectoralis region
parts.description: A surface overlay indicates the upper chest beneath the anatomical bodysuit. The continuous shoulders and clavicles connect the torso to the arms.

parts.name: Back
parts.description: The posterior trunk joins the shoulders, waist and pelvis. Hair fades while you inspect this region so the true back surface is visible; the highlight and label follow the same skinned surface during rotation.

parts.name: Pelvis
parts.description: The pelvic region connects the waist and hips to the thighs. The mint highlight marks the covered surface rather than exposed internal anatomy.
